title: Systems programming in C
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Program close to the machine in C: types, operators and control flow, functions, headers and the build process, pointers and arrays, strings, structs, dynamic memory with malloc and free, debugging with gdb and Valgrind, linked structures, file I/O, Unix processes and system calls, and avoiding undefined behavior.

weeks.1: C basics: types, operators and control flow
weeks.2: Functions, headers and how C programs are built
weeks.7: Dynamic memory: malloc, free and the heap
weeks.8: Memory bugs and tools: gdb and Valgrind
weeks.11: The Unix process model and system calls

blocks.deliverable: Write and compile three C programs.
Trace pointer programs by drawing memory.
Week 7 midterm; find and fix the memory bugs in a supplied program.
Implement a linked list in C.
Design a small shell that runs commands.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Implement a C program of 400–800 lines, such as a key-value store, a text-processing utility or a tiny shell, with a Makefile, tests and a clean Valgrind run, plus a written explanation of its memory management.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
